summary: This informational document asks that RFC 2754 be moved to Historic status. That RFC asked IANA to create and digitally sign routing registry objects when assigning addresses, to distribute a public key. In practice this was never done on the public Internet.

plainLanguage.summary: An old rule said an address-handing office should sign certain records. They never did, so this asks for the rule to be marked old.

subtitle: IANA is told not to sign routing registry objects as RFC 2754 requested, and that RFC moves to Historic.

tldr.problem: RFC 2754 asked IANA to create and digitally sign RPSL objects, including for each address assignment, but this was never done on the public Internet.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6254 obsoletes RFC 2754, recommends Historic status, and directs IANA not to pursue the actions in it.
tldr.outcome: RPKI technologies now provide an architecture for secure routing, so implementing the old actions would add significant complexity.

facts.label: IANA instruction
facts.value: Do not pursue the RFC 2754 actions

today: RFC 6254 is an Informational memo that obsoletes RFC 2754 and recommends Historic status for it. It has not been obsoleted itself.

sections.title: What RFC 2754 Asked For
sections.content:
RFC 2754 requested that the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) create a repository of Routing Policy Specification Language (RPSL) objects and digitally sign them. It named the initial objects and asked that each time IANA makes an address assignment, it also create new objects as needed (inetnum and as-block objects) and sign them. The aim was to distribute the IANA-held public key in software implementations of the Distributed Routing Policy System.

In practice this was never done on the public Internet. A review of RFCs in 2009 made that clear.
sections.plainLanguage: An old rule told the address office to stamp its records with a signature. The office never did it.

sections.title: Why It Is Historic
sections.content:
The memo notes that another technology appears to be taking the role once envisioned for Distributed RPSL. An architecture and infrastructure now exist for secure routing using Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI), and the semantics of a Route Origin Authorization (ROA) for validating route origination have been standardized by the IETF.

Implementing the old IANA actions would now require significant implementation complexity. So the document obsoletes RFC 2754, recommends Historic status, and directs IANA not to move forward with the actions in it.
sections.plainLanguage: A better signing system was built since then, so doing the old plan now would be extra work for nothing.

sections.title: Terms and IANA Instructions
sections.content:
The memo defines two words. An allocation is a block of addresses managed by a registry for the purpose of making assignments and allocations. An assignment is a block of addresses, or a single address, registered to an end-user for use on a specific network or set of networks.

The IANA instruction is short: IANA is instructed not to pursue or implement the IANA actions requested in RFC 2754. Because the signing never took place, moving RFC 2754 to Historic has no known impact on the security of the Internet.
sections.plainLanguage: An allocation is a big plot of land given to a manager. An assignment is the plot a specific person gets to use. IANA is told: forget the old signing job.

references.text: Alaettinoglu, C., Villamizar, C., and R. Govindan, "RPS IANA Issues", RFC 2754, January 2000.
